questions.stem: A new drug Eluxadoline is used in adults for the treatment of irritable bowel syndrome with diarrhea. Eluxadoline is a ?
questions.solutionHtml:
Mu-opioid receptor agonist
  • Eluxadoline: it is a mu-opioid receptor agonist, kappa opioid receptor agonist, and a delta opioid receptor antagonist. Eluxadoline is used for diarrhea-predominant IBS because it reduces intestinal contractility and normalizes stress-induced acceleration of upper GI transit.

  • Fedotozine:
    • Peripheral k-receptor selective antagonist
    • Devoid of CNS side effects
    • Used in IBS-diarrhea predominant


Goodman & Gilman's: The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page Number: 934

questions.stem: A cancer patient was taking morphine for pain. He had chronic constipation and used many laxatives but without any improvement. The best drug for this patient is?
questions.solutionHtml:
Methylnaltrexone
  • Peripheral mu Opioid antagonist
  • No analgesic effect
  • FDA approved for the treatment of opioid-induced constipationin patients receiving palliative care when laxative therapy is insufficient
  • Linaclotide
  • Guanylate cyclase agonist
  • Treatment of chronic constipation and irritable bowel syndrome with constipation
  • Plecanatide: (Jan. 2017)
  • Approved for the treatment of chronic idiopathic constipation in adults
  • It is a guanylate cyclase-C(GC-C) agonist
  • Lubiprostone
  • A bicyclic fatty acid metabolite analog of prostaglandin E1 activates type-2-chloride channels
  • Used in the treatment of chronic constipation in adults and irritable bowel syndrome with constipation (IBS-C) in adult women.

questions.stem: The drug used in irritable bowel syndrome with constipation is?
questions.solutionHtml:
Linaclotide

Linaclotide is Chloride Channel-2 Activator, Increasing liquid secretion in the gut and decreasing transit time, therefore used for chronic constipation. It has also been approved for constipation-dominant irritable bowel syndrome in women.

questions.stem: A 23-year-old man traveling on vacation in the Maldives noted some mild abdominal cramps and three or four unformed stools over the past 24 hours. No blood was seen in the stool. Which of the following drugs would be appropriate to treat the patient's diarrhea?
questions.solutionHtml:
Bismuth subsalicylate
  • Reason-B The patient is most likely affected by travelers’ diarrhea, which typically begins within 24 to 48 hours after eating focally contaminated food. Several Enterobacteriaceae can cause travelers’ diarrhea, varying according to the area of travel.

  • Bismuth subsalicylate is effective in patients with diarrhea caused by E. coli, Helicobacter pylori, Campylobacter jejune, and Salmonella species and also inhibits enteric secretions.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number:-733

questions.stem: A 34-year-old man was admitted to the hospital because of prolonged, massive watery diarrhea for the past 2 days. Physical and lab exams indicated a pancreatic tumor, and radioimmunoassay confirmed the diagnosis of VIPoma. The patient was given intravenous fluids for hydration and was scheduled for surgery. Which of the following drugs would be appropriate to control the patient's diarrhea?
questions.solutionHtml:
Octreotide

Reason-Octreotide is a somatostatin analog. When given in pharmacological amounts, somatostatin inhibits virtually all exocrine and endocrine secretions of the pancreas (insulin, glucagon, and pancreatic enzymes), stomach (gastrin), and intestine (secretin, motilin, vasoactive intestinal polypeptide [VIP], gastric inhibitory polypeptide [GIP], and serotonin), as well as secretion of growth hormone, thyroid-stimulating hormone, parathyroid hormone, calcitonin, and adrenocorticotropic hormone. Because of this, octreotide is used to reduce symptoms caused by a variety of hormone-secreting tumors.



Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 733
